input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that "Apple's increased research and development spending weighed on its operating margin in the quarter ended March 28, 2026."

The numeric check definitively shows that operating margin INCREASED from 31.0% in Q2 2025 to 32.3% in Q2 2026 (calculated as operating income of $35,885M divided by net sales of $111,184M for Q2 2026, versus $29,589M / $95,359M for Q2 2025).

While the claim is correct that R&D spending increased significantly (34% year-over-year from $8,550M to $11,419M), this did NOT weigh on operating margin. Instead, operating margin expanded by 1.3 percentage points.

The evidence shows that gross margin improvements from product mix and favorable currency effects (E2, E15) more than offset the increase in operating expenses including R&D. The gross margin percentage increased from 47.1% to 49.3% (E2), which provided sufficient expansion to absorb the higher R&D spending (which increased from 9% to 10% of sales) and still deliver operating margin expansion.

Therefore, the claim is factually incorrect - operating margin improved rather than being weighed down, making this CONTRADICTED.
